title: WPSS/1029/2013 of Daya Ram Yadav Vs Bharat Heavy Electrical Limited AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1029 of 2013
Daya Ram Yadav ÖÖ Petitioner
Versus
Bharat Heavy Electrical Limited & others ÖÖ.. Respondents
Present: Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
 Mr. V.K. Kohali, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Rajni
Supyal, Advocate for the respondents.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner applied for the post of Furnace
Operator in Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, which is
Government of India Corporation. The recruitment is of the
year 2009. The petitioner, who was not selected filed the
Writ Petition No.1594 (S/S) of 2012, which was disposed by
this Court vide order dated 08.05.2013, which reads as
under:-
 ìI have heard learned counsel for the
parties. I dispose of the writ petition directing
respondent No. 2 i.e. General Manager (HR),
Bharat Heavy Electrical Limited, Haridwar to
treat a copy of the writ petition as
representation and decide the same upon
hearing the petitioner. After hearing the
matter, he shall pass a speaking order.
 Entire exercise shall be completed
within a period of eight weeks from the date
of communication of this order.
 Let a copy of the writ petition and
certified copy of this order be forwarded to the
above Officer.î
2. Consequently, the matter of the petitioner was
heard by the General Manager (HR), Bharat Heavy
Electrical Limited, Haridwar who has rejected the

2
representation of the petitioner by order dated 20.06.2013.
Aggrieved, petitioner has filed present writ petition.
3. The impugned order has been perused. As per
the terms of the advertisement, the requirement for the
post of Furnace Operator was that one must have five years
of work experience of secondary steel melting in Electric
Arc Furnace of minimum 30 ton. In order to match up five
years of experience one must have done 1500 days of work
as above.
4. The entire experience of the petitioner,
according to the Committee constituted for verifying the
work experience of candidates is only 1218 days of
experience. Not only this the petitioner has also crossed the
maximum age limit.
5. Indeed there is a provision in the
advertisement for relaxation of age limit, considering that
petitioner belongs to an Other Backward Classes
community candidate but in order to get that relaxation
one must have put additional work experience of 972 days.
Therefore, the total work experience required from the
petitioner is 2472 days, but petitioner has only 1218 days
of experience.
6. It is true that the petitioner has filed a
Certificate of experience, which states that the petitioner
has worked for higher duration of time than what the
respondents have determined. Regarding this, it has been
stated by the General Manager (BHEL) that the Certificate
was subject to the verification and scrutiny and after

3
verification and scrutiny of this certificate, the Committee
came to the conclusion that only 1218 days are verified.
7. In view thereof since the petitioner did not
fulfill the eligibility requirement, hence, no fault can be
found in the order dated 20.06.2013. The writ petition fails
and is hereby dismissed.
8. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 10.03.2015
 Nitesh
